page: The Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on the x86_64 architecture at 3.7 GHz. The instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration.

The D4as_v6 does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the AMD core architecture delivers strong single-core compute performance, as shown in top-quartile results for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside high text-processing scores. However, multi-core throughput, static web serving, and PassMark computational tests reflect middle-of-the-pack performance. Heavy uncached memory operations and compiler workloads such as Clang compilation trend toward the lower quartile, corresponding to moderate memory bandwidth metrics.

Given the absence of local disks and the high single-thread execution speed, the D4as_v6 offers balanced resource efficiency for standard compute environments without demanding extreme I/O. Appropriate workloads include middle-tier web application serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, text manipulation pipelines, and small-scale lightweight caching or inference services. Data-heavy transactional databases and memory-intensive distributed processing may encounter bottlenecks due to memory read speeds and external disk latency.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It features no local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for persistent data. Benchmark profiles demonstrate strong single-thread performance in stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput, uncached memory bandwidth, and Clang compilation metrics align within average to lower tiers. The absence of local scratch space and lower database transaction rates suggest caution for IO-heavy storage setups. Consequently, the instance is well matched for web application hosting, API endpoints, microservices, lightweight machine learning inference, and general enterprise application processing.
